sn11.7:1.2: “Bhikkhus, once in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was alone in seclusion, the following reflection arose in his mind:
sn11.7:1.3: ‘Though someone may be my sworn enemy, I should not transgress even against him.’
sn11.7:1.4: “Then, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, having known with his own mind the reflection in Sakka’s mind, approached Sakka, lord of the devas.
sn11.7:1.5: Sakka saw Vepacitti coming in the distance and said to him:
sn11.7:2.1: ‘Dear sir, do not abandon the idea that just occurred to you.’—
sn11.7:3.1: ‘Swear, Vepacitti, that you won’t transgress against me.’
sn11.7:4.1:
Vepacitti:
‘“Whatever evil comes to a liar,
sn11.7:4.2: Whatever evil to a reviler of noble ones,
sn11.7:4.3: Whatever evil to a betrayer of friends,
sn11.7:4.4: Whatever evil to one without gratitude:
sn11.7:4.5: That same evil touches the one
sn11.7:4.6: Who transgresses against you, Suja’s husband.’”
